skill.name: pytest-mock-guide
skill.description: Guide for using pytest-mock to write Python tests with mocking, patching, spying, stubbing, async mocks, and assertion helpers.
skill.summary: Use pytest-mock patterns to patch dependencies, inspect calls, and write clearer Python tests.
skill.author: bossjones

static_findings.snippet: pytest-mock is a pytest plugin providing a `mocker` fixture as a thin wrapper around Python's `unitt
The `mocker` fixture is the main interface. Request it in your test function:
| `class_mocker` | class | Share mocks across test class |
| `module_mocker` | module | Share mocks across test module |
| `session_mocker` | session | Share mocks across entire session |
Same as `patch.object` but doesn't warn when mock is used as context manager:
| `return_value` | Value returned when mock is called |
| `side_effect` | Exception to raise or function to call |
| `spec_set` | Stricter spec that prevents setting new attributes |
| `spy_return` | Last return value from real method |

content.value_statement: Mocking in pytest can be confusing when patch targets, spies, and assertions differ. This skill gives concise patterns for pytest-mock fixtures, patches, stubs, and async tests.
actual_capabilities: Explains the mocker fixture and scoped variants for pytest tests.
Shows patch, patch.object, patch.dict, patch.multiple, and context-manager patching.
Documents spy, stub, async_stub, autospec, and direct mock helper patterns.
Lists call and await assertion helpers with pytest-style introspection.
Provides examples for async functions, exceptions, properties, and patching where used.
limitations: It is a written guide, not a runnable test generator.
Examples use placeholder modules and need adaptation to each codebase.
It does not install pytest-mock or modify project configuration.
It does not validate mocks against live application behavior.

use_cases.title: Mock Service Dependencies
use_cases.description: Plan pytest tests that replace database, cache, API, or file dependencies with controlled mocks.

use_cases.title: Review Test Patterns
use_cases.description: Check whether tests patch the correct target and assert calls with useful precision.

use_cases.title: Teach pytest-mock Basics
use_cases.description: Use compact examples to explain fixtures, spies, stubs, autospec, and async assertions.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Mocker Fixture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pytest-mock-guide to explain when to use the mocker fixture and how cleanup works.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Patch Method
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pytest-mock-guide to choose the right patch method for a function, object attribute, dictionary, or several attributes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Mock Assertions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pytest-mock-guide to plan assertions for calls, awaits, side effects, and exceptions in my pytest test.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Existing Test Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pytest-mock-guide to review my pytest tests for patch-target mistakes, missing autospec, brittle mock chains, and weak assertions.

output_examples.input: I need to patch a dependency imported into my module.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends patching the symbol where it is used, then asserting the mocked call. It explains why patching the original module can miss imported references.

output_examples.input: I need to test an async callback.
output_examples.output: The skill points to async_stub or AsyncMock, await assertions, and async side-effect patterns.
The skill suggests autospec or spec_set to catch signature errors and unexpected attributes.

best_practices: Patch the symbol where production code looks it up.
Use autospec or spec_set when interface drift would hide defects.
Prefer clear call assertions over broad assertions on mock existence.
anti_patterns: Patching the library definition when the code under test imports a local reference.
Building long mock chains without checking behavior at meaningful boundaries.
Using unrestricted mocks when interface accuracy matters.

faq.question: What is pytest-mock?
faq.answer: pytest-mock is a pytest plugin that provides a mocker fixture around unittest.mock APIs.

faq.question: Does this skill execute tests?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation for writing tests and does not run commands or modify files.

faq.question: When should I use mocker.patch.object?
faq.answer: Use it when you already have the target object and need to replace one attribute.

faq.question: How do spies differ from mocks?
faq.answer: A spy calls the real function while recording calls, return values, and exceptions.

faq.question: Does it cover async tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes async stubs, AsyncMock usage, await assertions, and async iterator examples.

faq.question: Can it help with flaky mocks?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains patch target selection, cleanup, reset behavior, and stricter mock specifications.
